newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. stock index futures end choppy trade up.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. stock index futures end choppy trade up.

text.p: Most U.S. stock index futures popped up again during the last five minutes of trading and finished pit trading firmer.
Traders tied the final spike back up to a bout of short-covering after December Standard & Poor's (S&P) 500 futures probed the downside late but lacked followthrough.
"That was a short squeeze -- evening up of positions going into the weekend," one floor broker said of the late rebound.
The contract, which had found support from gains in U.S. Treasury bond futures, slumped during the last hour to a new day's low and pierced support at the 703.50 level.
Some tied that drop to position-evening as well, as day longs decided to even up after the morning's rise stalled.
"I think it's just more of a correction," one floor broker said of the afternoon pullback to unchanged. "Earlier this morning, we got a few bargain-hunters in here."
After Thursday's technically weak performance, when December S&P 500s broke support at 704.50 and 704.10, some traders had predicted more losses early on Friday.
But after briefly probing the downside at the open, the contract bounced up from support at 703.50 and rallied as U.S. Treasury bond futures advanced.

T-bond futures, which slipped on stronger than expected durable goods orders, got a boost from weaker than forecast existing home sales. But December S&P 500s futures still failed to clear additional resistance at 708.35.
Traders noted some signs that a few arbitrage sell programs took advantage of the narrow opening premium to cash.

Fair value on Friday stood at roughly 3.30 points premium, based on the London Interbank Offered Rate. Arbitrage buy programs needed a premium of 4.00 points or more. Sell programs would have required a premium of about 2.60 points over cash or less.
Friday's turnover was estimated at about 70,000 December S&P 500s compared to Thursday's cleared volume of 78,905.

Nikkei 225 index futures drew good selling from one dealer and stayed below 21,000.00, although one floor chartist said that level was not significant. He thought Nikkei futures were due to turn higher again and challenge 23,200.00 level.

December S&P 500 settled up 1.60 points at 705.35, Value Lines rose 2.40 points to 648.00, Nikkei 225 fell 90.0 to 20,820.0, Midcap 400s firmed 0.60 to 244.75, and NYSE Composite added 0.85 point to 375.20. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
